title: Sample Values by Weight
prompt:
Implement `WeightedSampler(values, weights, rng=random.random)`. Each `sample()` call returns one value with probability proportional to its weight, independently of previous draws. Build cumulative weights once, then implement the lookup with your own binary search; do not call a library binary-search helper.

`values` and `weights` have the same nonzero length. Weights are finite, nonnegative numbers with a positive total. Zero-weight values must never be returned. `rng()` supplies a uniform number in `[0, 1)`; keep it injectable for deterministic checks. Assert the input preconditions. Explain preprocessing cost and cost per draw.

example.reasoning: The cumulative intervals are [0, 1) for A and [1, 4) for B; 0.6 times the total weight is 2.4.
